name: Swayambhunath Monkey Temple Sunrise Walk
description: You will ascend 365 ancient stone steps alongside resident macaques to reach this iconic hilltop stupa just as dawn breaks over the valley. The scent of burning incense and the rhythmic chanting of monks fill the air as you take in unobstructed panoramas of the sprawling city below. It provides a spiritual introduction to the capital's deeply intertwined Hindu and Buddhist heritage.
duration_note: Foreigner entrance fee of 200 NPR is collected at the base. Best visited before 7:00 AM to catch the clear morning light and active monastic rituals.

name: Pashupatinath Bagmati River Evening Aarti Ritual
description: You will sit across the sacred Bagmati River to witness the striking, deeply moving evening Bagmati Aarati ritual, where priests swing massive oil lamps in unison to hymns. As classical instruments echo, you will observe traditional open-air cremations on the opposite ghats, offering an unfiltered look into Hindu cycles of life and death. The atmospheric glow of oil lamps and spiritual energy makes this an unforgettable sensory experience.
duration_note: Foreigner entry fee is 1,000 NPR. Non-Hindus are strictly forbidden from entering the inner sanctum of the main temple but have full access to the riverbank viewing areas.

name: Patan Durbar Square Newari Architecture Walking Tour
description: You will walk through an open-air museum of exquisite red-brick palaces, wood-carved windows, and ancient stone temples representing the zenith of Newari craftsmanship. Guided by a local preservationist, you'll discover hidden courtyards, watch bronze-casting artisans, and tour the world-class Patan Museum housed inside the old royal palace. It is the perfect immersion into the artistic soul of the Kathmandu Valley.
duration_note: Foreigner entry fee is 1,000 NPR, which includes admission to the Patan Museum. Keep your ticket handy as it can be checked at multiple points in the square.

name: Traditional Newari Feast at Bhojan Griha
description: You will step into a restored 150-year-old royal building to indulge in a multi-course, authentic Newari feast served in traditional brass tableware. While sitting cross-legged on floor cushions, you will sample rich buffalo curries, spiced lentil patties (bara), and fiery smoked meats, accompanied by local rice wine (aila). Cultural folk dances from different ethnic groups perform live right before your table throughout the evening.
duration_note: Advance reservations are highly recommended during the peak tourist seasons of spring and autumn. Vegetarian options are readily available upon request.

name: Tibetan Momo and Khapse Culinary Crawl
description: You will navigate the bustling alleys surrounding the colossal white dome of Boudhanath Stupa to taste the culinary heritage of Nepal's Tibetan diaspora. Led by a local guide, you will sample steaming buffalo and vegetable momos at a hidden courtyard eatery, sip salted butter tea at a rooftop café, and crunch on sweet khapse pastries. The experience gives you an intimate understanding of how Himalayan food evolved in the valley.
duration_note: Includes the 400 NPR foreigner entrance fee to the Boudhanath stupa area. Best experienced in the late afternoon when the Tibetan community gathers for evening Kora circles.

name: Live Mountain Rock Jam Session at Purple Haze Rock Bar
description: You will immerse yourself in Kathmandu's surprisingly legendary rock music scene at this massive, high-energy venue in the heart of Thamel. Grab a local Gorkha beer and watch exceptionally talented local covers and original bands tear up the stage with everything from classic rock to metal. The packed crowd of international trekkers and young locals creates an electric, unifying atmosphere found nowhere else in South Asia.
duration_note: Bands usually take the stage around 8:00 PM. Entry fees may apply on Friday nights when headline Nepalese rock bands are performing.

name: Craft Cocktails at Phat Kath and Rooftop Lounging
description: You will wind down from a long day of sightseeing in this cozy, bohemian alleyway bar known for its incredible playlist, local art installations, and creative mixology. Sip on artisanal cocktails infused with Himalayan herbs and ginger while chatting with seasoned mountaineers and expats. It offers a relaxed alternative to Thamel's louder clubs, perfect for an intimate evening of conversation.
duration_note: Happy hour runs daily from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Excellent selection of vegan-friendly bar snacks is available.

name: Sound Healing and Tibetan Singing Bowl Session
description: You will lie down in a serene, incense-scented studio while a master practitioner places hand-hammered Tibetan singing bowls directly on your body's energy centers. As the bowls are struck and rubbed, the deep, resonant vibrations and harmonic frequencies wash over you, clearing mental chatter and inducing a state of deep meditation. It is an intensely therapeutic way to reset after a strenuous Himalayan trek or a chaotic city tour.
duration_note: Wear loose, comfortable clothing. Loose metal jewelry should be removed before the session to prevent interference with the bowl vibrations.

name: Day Hike to Nagi Gumba Buddhist Nunnery
description: You will hike through dense subtropical forests of oak and rhododendron up the northern rim of the Kathmandu Valley inside a protected reserve. Your destination is an isolated, active Buddhist nunnery perched on a mountain cliff, offering sweeping views of the valley and distant snow-capped peaks. You will have the unique chance to observe the daily lives, prayers, and traditional lifestyle of the resident nuns.
duration_note: Requires a Shivapuri National Park entry permit (1,000 NPR for foreigners), which must be purchased at the Budhanilkantha gate. Bring plenty of water and a light jacket as the ridge can get windy and cool.

name: The Classic Everest Base Camp Expedition
description: You will embark on the ultimate pilgrimage in the trekking world, foot-slogging through breathtaking alpine valleys, crossing swinging suspension bridges draped in prayer flags, and staying in remote Sherpa villages. You'll climb the iconic viewpoint of Kala Patthar at 5,545 meters to watch the sunrise turn Mount Everest a brilliant gold before standing on the historic Khumbu Glacier at Base Camp itself. It is a grueling yet profoundly life-altering test of endurance.
location: Lukla to Everest Base Camp, Khumbu
duration_note: Requires Sagarmatha National Park Permit (3,000 NPR) and Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Municipality Permit (2,000 NPR). Mandatory guide rules apply. High risk of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS); itinerary must include acclimatization days at Namche and Dingboche. Flights from Kathmandu/Ramechhap to Lukla are notoriously prone to severe weather delays; build in 3 flexible buffer days.

name: Gokyo Lakes & Cho La Pass High Altitude Trek
description: You will trek off the beaten path to the spectacular, sapphire-blue glacial lakes of the Gokyo Valley, sitting under the shadow of Cho Oyu. You'll climb Gokyo Ri (5,357m) for a superior panoramic view of four 8,000-meter peaks, then strap on microspikes to conquer the steep, icy boulder fields of the treacherous Cho La Pass. This route offers a wilder, less-crowded alternative to the standard Base Camp trail.
location: Gokyo Valley and Cho La Pass, Khumbu
duration_note: Requires Sagarmatha National Park Permit (3,000 NPR) and Khumbu Municipality Permit (2,000 NPR). Crossing the Cho La Pass requires basic mountaineering gear (microspikes/crampons) and should not be attempted during or immediately after heavy snowfall.

name: Tengboche Monastery Morning Buddhist Blessing
description: You will step inside the highest active Buddhist monastery in the Khumbu region, set against a jaw-dropping backdrop of Ama Dablam and Mount Everest. Sit quietly in the ornate, tapestry-lined prayer hall as horns blare and monks beat heavy drums during their mystical morning chanting rituals. You can receive a personal silk khata blessing from the high lama for safe passage through the treacherous mountain passes.
duration_note: No entrance fee, but a small donation (500-1,000 NPR) to the monastery maintenance fund is strongly customary. Dress modestly in long layers and remove shoes and hats before entering the main shrine hall. Photography is strictly forbidden inside during prayers.

name: Yak Steak and Sherpa Stew Dinner at Café de 8848
description: You will celebrate reaching the sherpa capital of 3,440 meters by ordering a sizzling, protein-packed wild yak steak served on a hot iron platter. Pair it with Syakpa, a traditional, deeply comforting Sherpa potato stew loaded with hand-pulled dough and alpine herbs designed to combat the high-altitude chill. While dining, you can watch historic black-and-white documentaries about early Everest climbs projected on the cafe walls.
duration_note: Prices reflect the high cost of transporting ingredients up the mountain by yak or porter. Yak meat is lean and dense; specify your cooking preference carefully.

name: High Altitude Irish Pub Night at The Irish Pub Namche
description: You will claim a stool at the officially recognized highest Irish Pub in the world, sitting at a dizzying 3,440 meters above sea level. Swap wild trail stories with international trekkers, guides, and elite Sherpa climbers while throwing darts and listening to classic rock. Warm up with a hot toddy or a pint of Guinness while enjoying the surreal vibe of a fully stocked Irish bar deep in the Himalayas.
duration_note: Alcohol hits significantly harder and increases dehydration risks at this altitude; consume responsibly, especially if you have ascent plans the following morning.

name: Everest Luxury Helicopter Tour with Kala Patthar Landing
description: You will skip the weeks of grueling trekking and board a high-altitude helicopter from Kathmandu, soaring directly over the dramatic ridges of the Khumbu. You'll touch down briefly on the rocky ledge of Kala Patthar (5,545m) for an elite, face-to-face view of Everest's south face that very few humans ever see. Afterward, land at the world-famous Hotel Everest View for a Champagne breakfast on an open-air terrace overlooking the peaks.
duration_note: Operates strictly in the early mornings when mountain weather is clearest. Ground time at 5,545m is limited to 15 minutes max to prevent severe acute altitude sickness due to the rapid ascent.

name: Khumjung Village Exploration and Yeti Scalp Viewing
description: You will walk through the peaceful, green-walled stone fields of Khumjung village, a traditional Sherpa settlement largely untouched by commercial tourism. Visit the local monastery to see the famous, strictly guarded 'Yeti Scalp' kept inside an iron safe by the village elders. Afterward, walk down to the historic Hillary School, established by Sir Edmund Hillary to give back to the communities that made his summit possible.
duration_note: The monastery asks for a small donation (approx. 300 NPR) to open the yeti relic box for foreign tourists. Can easily be done as an acclimatization day-trip from Namche Bazaar.

name: Sarangkot Sunrise Paragliding Over Fewa Lake
description: You will sprint off a grassy mountain ridge at Sarangkot alongside an experienced tandem pilot, launching directly into thermal updrafts. Soar eye-to-eye with the jagged, snow-capped peaks of the Annapurna Range and the iconic fishtail peak of Machapuchare. The flight finishes with a thrilling series of wingovers before a gentle landing on the shores of sapphire-blue Fewa Lake.
duration_note: Strictly subject to wind and weather conditions. Weight limits generally apply between 45kg and 100kg. Booking includes mandatory insurance and Go-Pro video/photos.

name: The Annapurna Circuit Trek & Thorong La Pass Challenge
description: You will journey through one of the most diverse long-distance trails on earth, climbing from lush subtropical rice paddies to the barren, wind-scoured Tibetan landscape of Mustang. Push your physical limits on the brutal, pre-dawn climb up Thorong La Pass, standing victorious at 5,416 meters amidst frozen glaciers. Descend into the sacred pilgrimage oasis of Muktinath, completing an epic crossing of the massive Annapurna massif.
location: Besisahar to Jomsom via Thorong La Pass
duration_note: Requires Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) Permit (3,000 NPR) and a TIMS card. Route requires mandatory certified guide tracking. Proper high-altitude cold weather gear and acclimatization in Manang are non-negotiable.

name: Ghorepani Poon Hill Panorama Trek
description: You will climb up thousands of hand-carved stone steps through enchanting, ancient rhododendron forests that explode in shades of pink and red during spring. On the final morning, hike up to the summit of Poon Hill (3,210m) in the dark to witness a stunning, wide-angle sunrise over the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges. It is the absolute best short, low-altitude trek for travelers short on time but hungry for Himalayan vistas.
duration_note: Requires ACAP Permit (3,000 NPR). While altitude sickness is rare here, the steep uphill stairclimbs require a moderate baseline level of physical fitness.

name: Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddleboarding on Fewa Lake
description: You will rent a sleek, brightly colored kayak or a paddleboard to explore the tranquil western reaches of Pokhara's central lake, far from the tourist strip. Paddle across the glassy waters to the small island temple of Tal Barahi, watching Hindu devotees arrive on wooden longboats. On a clear day, the entire Annapurna mountain range reflects perfectly on the lake surface around your craft.
duration_note: Wearing the provided life jacket is legally mandatory at all times on the water. Avoid paddling during late afternoons when strong winds can cause sudden waves.

name: White-Water Rafting the Roaring Upper Seti River
description: You will tackle non-stop, adrenaline-pumping Class III and IV rapids on a half-day whitewater run down a narrow volcanic gorge. With the snow-covered peak of Machapuchare looming upstream, you and your professional paddle team will crash through technical drops like 'Landslide' and 'Sweet 16.' It delivers an intense, continuous rush of white-water action just a short drive from Pokhara city.
duration_note: Participants must know how to swim. Operates primarily from September to May; rapids can become dangerously extreme and close during the peak monsoon summer months.

name: Thakali Khana Culinary Experience at Fresh Elements
description: You will taste the absolute gold standard of Nepal's national dish, Dal Bhat, perfected by the Thakali people of the Mustang region. Your brass platter features aromatic local rice, slow-cooked black lentil soup, spiced mustard greens, local ghee, and incredibly flavorful wild wild-boar or chicken curry. Top it off with their signature spicy radish pickle and roasted buckwheat flour toppings for an authentic depth of flavor.
duration_note: Dal Bhat features complimentary unlimited refills on all components except the primary meat portion—simply ask the server for more rice or lentils.

name: Lakefront Cocktails and Campfires at Busy Bee Café
description: You will slide into an open-air wooden booth at Pokhara's most legendary nightlife institution, where live acoustic and rock bands play every single night. Sip cold local beers or signature ginger-honey cocktails around cozy brick fire pits in the outdoor garden. It serves as the ultimate living room for global backpackers celebrating the successful completion of long Annapurna treks.
duration_note: Gets extremely busy after 9:00 PM on weekends. The kitchen serves excellent wood-fired pizzas late into the night.

name: Himalayan Yoga and Meditation Retreat at Purna Yoga
description: You will spend a rejuvenating day at a tranquil hilltop retreat overlooking the quiet waters of Fewa Lake and the mountains. Participate in guided Hatha yoga flows, targeted breathing workshops (pranayama), and a deep sound-bath meditation led by expert local yogis. Fuel your body with organic, farm-to-table vegetarian meals prepared specifically to balance your internal energy.
duration_note: Includes round-trip jeep transfers from the main Lakeside hotel zone. No previous yoga experience is required; options can scale up to multi-week certified courses.

name: Deep Jungle Walking Safari and Tiger Tracking
description: You will venture deep into the dense sal forests and tall elephant-grass plains on foot, accompanied by two expert, stick-wielding jungle naturalists. Step softly as you track the footprints of the elusive Bengal tiger, spot rare Indian one-horned rhinoceroses cooling off in mud wallows, and watch wild elephants from camouflaged lookouts. Moving without a vehicle provides a raw, highly thrilling connection to the wild.
duration_note: Requires Chitwan National Park Entry Permit (2,000 NPR + VAT). Strict safety rules apply: you must stay behind your guides at all times, wear neutral earthy colors, and avoid running if large wildlife approaches.

name: Remote Wilderness Jeep Safari in Search of Wild Tigers
description: You will explore the wild, uncrowded riverine tracks of Nepal's largest and most remote lowland park in an open-top 4x4 vehicle. Because Bardia sees a fraction of Chitwan's tourists, your chances of spotting wild Bengal tigers, giant herds of wild elephants, and rare gangetic river dolphins along the Karnali River are exceptionally high. Spend hours quietly waiting at strategic riverbank blinds where apex predators come down to drink.
duration_note: Bardia park entry fee is 1,500 NPR for foreigners. Best visited between October and April when dry weather forces animals out toward major waterholes.

name: Sacred Garden Pilgrimage at Buddha's Birthplace
description: You will walk through the tranquil, UNESCO-protected Sacred Garden to stand at the exact birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (Lord Buddha). Explore the ancient archaeological ruins of the Mayadevi Temple, inspect the historic 3rd-century BC Ashoka Pillar, and sit beneath sprawling Bodhi trees draped in thousands of multi-colored prayer flags. The immense spiritual serenity makes it a cornerstone site for global peace and contemplation.
duration_note: Foreigner entrance fee is 200 NPR. Shoes must be removed before stepping onto the archaeological boardwalk inside the Mayadevi Temple; socks are permitted.

name: Traditional Dugout Canoe Crocodile Safari
description: You will glide silently down the misty waters of the Rapti River in a long, hand-carved wooden canoe hollowed out from a single tree trunk. Drift mere meters away from massive, sun-basking Gharial crocodiles—a critically endangered, fish-eating species with incredibly long, narrow snouts. Along the riverbanks, you'll also spot brilliant storks, kingfishers, and occasionally rhinos coming down for an evening bath.
duration_note: Often paired directly as a morning preface to a jungle walking or jeep safari. Keep your hands inside the canoe walls at all times due to crocodile presence.

name: Tharu Village Traditional Dinner and Ghongi Tasting
description: You will visit an authentic mud-and-thatch homestead of the indigenous Tharu people to sample food deeply connected to the lowland rivers and wetlands. Taste Ghongi, fresh freshwater snails clean-boiled and cooked in a rich, heavily spiced flaxseed sauce, eaten by sucking the meat directly from the shell. Your meal also includes steamed rice cakes (chaku) and local wild greens, offering a distinct departure from typical mountain cuisine.
duration_note: Eating snails requires a specific technique that your hosts will proudly demonstrate. Hand-washing facilities are provided as this meal is eaten entirely by hand.

name: Riverside Sundowners at Ken's Bamboo Bar
description: You will sit on a rustic bamboo stool directly on the banks of the Rapti River, listening to the distant nighttime calls of the jungle. Sip a refreshing cocktail or a cold Rhino beer while watching an incredible, unhindered sunset paint the tropical waters in deep oranges and purples. It is the premier gathering spot for safari-goers to relax, share wildlife photos, and chill out to laid-back reggae tunes.
duration_note: Mosquitoes are highly active near the river at dusk; application of high-DEET insect repellent is highly recommended before arrival.

name: Langtang Valley Recovery and Glacier Trek
description: You will hike through a deep, dramatic river gorge that opens up into an incredible alpine valley surrounded by soaring, ice-clad walls. Walk through Langtang Village, entirely rebuilt by its resilient community after the historic 2015 earthquake, and experience deep Tamang hospitality. Push up to Kyanjin Gompa to sample fresh yak cheese made right at the alpine factory before looking out over ice falls.
duration_note: Requires Langtang National Park Entry Permit (3,000 NPR) and a TIMS card. Government regulations mandate trekking with a licensed guide. The drive from Kathmandu to the Syabrubesi trailhead takes 7-9 hours over exceptionally bumpy mountain roads.

name: Sacred Alpine Gosaikunda Holy Lakes Trek
description: You will climb steeply out of the treeline into a harsh, high-altitude landscape to stand before a cluster of spectacular, crystal-clear alpine lakes. Gosaikunda sits at 4,380 meters and is revered by both Hindus and Buddhists as the creation of Lord Shiva. You will stay in basic stone teahouses on the lake edge, watching pilgrims pray along the icy shores under a massive canopy of stars.
duration_note: Requires Langtang National Park Entry Permit (3,000 NPR). The rapid altitude gain from Dhunche (1,960m) to Gosaikunda (4,380m) requires a slow pace and deliberate hydration to prevent AMS.

name: Kyanjin Ri Peak Dawn Alpine Ascent
description: You will wake up in the freezing pre-dawn dark to scramble up a steep, rocky ridge rising directly behind the settlement of Kyanjin Gompa. As you reach the prayer-flag-draped summit of Kyanjin Ri (4,773m), the sun illuminates the massive ice walls of Langtang Lirung and Kimshung. It delivers a full, uninterrupted 360-degree mountain amphitheater view with minimal technical climbing difficulty.
duration_note: Requires zero technical climbing gear, but trekking poles and microspikes are highly recommended if winter snow remains on the steep trail.

name: Artisanal Yak Cheese Tasting at Kyanjin Factory
description: You will visit an authentic, Swiss-assisted alpine cheese processing facility operating at 3,870 meters above sea level. Watch local cheesemakers process fresh, rich milk collected from high-altitude yak herds grazing on alpine herbs. You'll sample varying maturations of sharp, nutty, and dense yak cheese cut straight from massive aging wheels stored in cold stone cellars.
duration_note: The factory operates fully during production months from July to November. Vacuum-sealed blocks are available to buy, providing a perfect high-energy snack for your trek.

name: Hyolmo Culture Experience in Melamchi Gaon
description: You will explore the traditional, stone-paved villages of the isolated Helambu region to discover the unique heritage of the Hyolmo people. Visit historic, beautifully painted wooden monasteries containing ancient Buddhist scrolls, and observe intricate wood-carving practices. Stay with a local family in a homestay setting, participating in daily tasks like grinding maize and tasting home-brewed millet beer (chang).
duration_note: Requires Shivapuri or Langtang entry permits depending on your exact walking approach route. Homestay facilities are simple, with shared eco-toilets and bucket showers.

name: The Upper Mustang Restricted Area Trek
description: You will cross into a surreal, wind-scoured high-altitude desert featuring towering red-rock cliffs, wind-carved caves, and ancient white-washed settlements. Journey along trade routes unchanged for centuries to enter the walled medieval city of Lo Manthang, the historic capital of the Kingdom of Lo. Here, Tibetan Buddhist culture has been completely preserved by decades of strict geographic isolation.
duration_note: Requires a strictly enforced Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permit costing 500 USD per person for the first 10 days, plus an ACAP permit. Independent trekking is banned; you must book via a registered company with a minimum of two travelers in the group.

name: Exploring the Ancient Sky Caves of Jhong
description: You will climb a system of secure wooden ladders to enter an incredible, five-story cliff-dwelling complex hand-carved directly into a sheer rock wall thousands of years ago. Explore interconnected burial chambers, living quarters, and meditation rooms, gazing out through rock windows over the barren Tibetan plateau. Archeologists still struggle to completely explain who built these massive sky-high cliff systems.
duration_note: Requires the active Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permit to access. Safe steps and ladders are installed, but individuals with extreme vertigo should exercise caution.

name: 15th-Century Monastery Restoration Tour
description: You will step inside the colossal, earth-walled monasteries of Thubchen and Jampa Chode to marvel at some of the finest surviving Tibetan Buddhist art on earth. Guided by a local curator, you will examine massive, gold-leafed clay deities and complex mandalas recently brought back to life by international art restorers. The scent of yak-butter lamps and the deep shadows evoke an intensely ancient, spiritual world.
duration_note: A local community conservation ticket (approx. 1,000 NPR) is required to enter the three main monasteries of Lo Manthang, which funds ongoing architectural restoration.

name: Marpha Village Apple Brandy and Pie Tasting
description: You will walk between the iconic, white-washed stone walls of Marpha village, famous as the fruit basket of the deep Kali Gandaki Gorge. Visit a traditional stone orchard house to sample fresh, organic apple pies, dried apple rings, and potent apple brandy distilled locally using mountain spring water. It offers a wonderfully sweet culinary oasis along an otherwise dusty Himalayan route.
duration_note: Accessible on the standard Annapurna Circuit or via jeep from Jomsom. The brandy is locally produced; small bottles are securely packaged for travel transit.

name: Spiritual Cleansing at the 108 Sacred Waterspouts
description: You will visit the high-altitude temple complex of Muktinath (3,710m), a site sacred to both Hindus and Buddhists representing liberation. Brave the cold mountain air to walk beneath the semi-circular wall of 108 sacred, carved brass waterspouts pouring freezing glacial water. Pilgrims run beneath them fully clothed to purify their karma, followed by a dip in two holy water pools right in front of the shrine.
duration_note: Requires ACAP permit. Dressing rooms are available nearby to change into dry clothes after running through the waterspouts. Be prepared for strong winds in the afternoon.

name: Kanyam Tea Estate Organic Plucking Tour
description: You will wander through rolling, mist-draped hills covered in perfectly manicured, emerald-green tea bushes overlooking the plains of India. Learn the delicate technique of hand-plucking the finest 'two leaves and a bud' alongside local estate workers. Afterward, tour the historic processing factory to see withering, rolling, and oxidation machinery before sitting down for an expert-led premium orthodox tea-tasting class.
duration_note: Best visited between March and November during active plucking seasons. Monsoons bring beautiful heavy mists but require sturdy footwear for muddy paths.

name: Kanchenjunga Wilderness North & South Base Camp Expedition
description: You will embark on a long, deeply challenging trek through the isolated eastern frontier of Nepal to stand before the colossal mass of Kanchenjunga, the world's third highest peak. Walk through dense rhododendron reserves inhabited by red pandas and cross high alpine meadows untouched by tea houses. Staying primarily in basic community homestays and tents, this expedition delivers an unmatched wilderness experience.
duration_note: Requires a Kanchenjunga Restricted Area Permit (20 USD per week) and a Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (3,000 NPR). Must be organized with a licensed agency and a minimum of two trekkers. Extreme wilderness conditions with long walking days.

name: Antu Danda Dawn Mountain Viewpoint
description: You will stand on a wooden viewing tower at 2,328 meters in the chilly pre-dawn dark, watching the sun rise directly out of the plains of Bengal. The morning light strikes the massive snow walls of Mount Kanchenjunga first, turning the mountain a deep crimson before lighting up the rolling green tea hills below. It is widely considered the most spectacular, clear sunrise panorama in all of eastern Nepal.
duration_note: Requires an early 4:30 AM departure from your Ilam lodge. Clear views are highly reliable during the dry autumn and spring months.

name: Tongba and Rai Culinary Night
description: You will spend an evening warming up with Tongba, the iconic alcoholic drink of the eastern hills. Fermented millet grains are packed into a traditional wooden or brass canister, filled with boiling water, and sipped through a perforated bamboo straw as it continually infuses. Pair it with spiced pork curries and wild mushroom preparations cooked using traditional Rai and Limbu family recipes.
duration_note: The hot water in your Tongba canister can be refilled up to three or four times by the tavern keeper before the fermented millet loses its potency.
